title: [Mouse Without Borders] Service mode: SYSTEM process leaks Token/Event/Thread handles at a constant rate (~10k handles/day)

judgment.rationale: Replace the stale helper-restart/timer attribution. The desktop/socket lifetime boundary is now the strongest discriminator, but the retaining allocator is still unknown. Measure the TCP-owning process across peer crossing and desktop teardown before selecting SafeHandle, thread-join or socket cleanup changes; flat live threads do not establish which retained handle owner is responsible.
evidence: The author's latest corrections supersede the earlier timer/helper-restart narrative: growth starts only after crossing to the peer and back, then persists while idle.
The reported cadence is roughly three Token, two Event and one Thread handles every 50 seconds in the SYSTEM process owning the TCP connection; live thread count stays flat.
A desktop switch releases the accumulated handles without changing the owning PID. The second SYSTEM/helper process remains stable.
Killing the helper does not reclaim the handles; growth continued for more than eleven hours without it. The author plans a current-version retest from the older 0.100.2 baseline.

Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Form/frmScreen.cs: HelperTimer_Tick tests desktop/session activity and calls sk.Close(false), clears Common.Sk and later permits socket recreation. This corroborates a real desktop-lifetime boundary, not the leaking allocation.

Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/SocketStuff.cs: SocketStuff owns client/server connection lifetimes and multiple socket worker paths. A close boundary can release retained objects even if allocation happened elsewhere.
Read the complete October 25 correction, including the same-PID and helper-absent controls; no handle trace or current-build reproduction was executed in this pass.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce Mouse Without Borders service handles behavior

fix_assessment.rationale: Conditional lightweight proposal, not an implementation-grade design. The new differential evidence narrows the lifetime boundary but does not identify an allocating call stack.

proposed_fixes.title: Identify and bound retained connection-lifetime handles after peer crossing
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: peer-crossing activates a connection/session worker path that retains native handle sets until desktop-driven socket teardown. The exact allocator and owner remain unmeasured; the corrected evidence contradicts helper restart as the release mechanism.
plan: Reproduce the no-crossing control and the cross-to-peer-and-back trigger while sampling the TCP-owning SYSTEM PID separately from the helper.
Attribute each growing handle set to its creation/retention stack; compare one desktop switch with a helper-only termination while preserving the original process.
Only after identifying the owner, enforce deterministic cleanup at that connection/session lifetime and test repeated crossings plus normal/exception/desktop-close paths.
verification: Current-build Token/Event/Thread handle counts remain bounded after repeated crossings and hours idle.
Desktop switching and reconnection preserve input sharing; helper termination is not assumed to be a repair.
The old helper-restart and 26-second claims are not used as regression expectations.

confidence.rationale: The new differential evidence narrows the lifetime boundary but does not identify an allocating call stack.

reproduce.title: Validate Mouse Without Borders service handles report
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable release; compare the reported version only in an isolated test environment if needed.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: Record PID, service/helper role, TCP ownership and object counts before crossing; establish an idle no-crossing control.
Cross to the peer and back once, then idle while recording roughly 50-second handle sets and live-thread counts.
Capture owning allocation/retention stacks in the growing process; compare helper-only exit with a desktop switch and record whether that same PID releases objects.
Repeat on current stable and compare the reported older version only in a controlled environment.
reproduce.expected_result: Either counts remain bounded or an attributed handle owner, trigger and lifetime release boundary are demonstrated.
